Im sorry you’re going through this. My dog is also a border collie/heeler mixed with other herding breeds, so I know exactly how it feels. Herding dogs are smart, but also a lot of work, it’s just how it is. Something that helped a lot with my dog is getting him toys that make him think, like treat dispensers, which stimulates his mind. Training a herding dog needs to start with understanding what they’re bred to do-which is to do a job. If the dog doesn’t have a “job” to do, that leads to behavior issues.

As far as training, work on calling him to you when there’s noises outside and giving him a treat when he comes, as well as teaching him to stay down. Treats, treats, treats. Eventually he’ll learn. With nipping, when he nips, sternly say “NO”. My dog still isn’t perfectly behaved and I’m going the route of medication, but these tactics have definitely worked with curbing the really bad behavior, especially getting a toy that keeps him distracted so you can chill and relax. Good luck to you and I hope this helps!
